correctness.rationale: For arbitrary distinct nodes the two Lagrange coefficients realize the exact worst-case norm through freely selectable complex phases. Trigonometric split into between-node and outside-node regions gives the exact two-parameter formula, including long arcs and boundary nodes. The lower bound max(sec x,sin(theta/2)/sin x) has a unique intersection x=arctan(sin(theta/2)); the center displacement adds a strictly positive outside penalty unless m=0. The unique centered pair realizes the bound. The proof handles all 0<theta<pi, all admissible node pairs, and both endpoint limits. 2400 finite pseudorandom node tests supplement but do not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The new uncountable family of two-dimensional complex function spaces has a canonical practical norm-recovery question: how accurately can two natural point evaluations replace the continuous arc supremum? The result gives the exact all-node distortion, the unique best two-sample geometry and a strictly monotone norming signature of the canonically represented function-space family. The optimal amplification stays below sqrt(2), whereas naive endpoint sampling diverges as theta tends to pi, yielding a substantive uniform-stability distinction. This is a complete natural exact invariant of a motivated function-space family, beyond a generic Lagrange computation; no downstream theorem is asserted or required.
